title: Apple set to take on Meta with smart glasses, may launch in 2027
summary: Apple plans 2027 launch for smart glasses to compete directly with Meta
detailed: Apple is developing its first smart glasses, internally code-named N50 and expected to debut around June 2027, featuring cameras, mics, speakers, and no AR display.
The hardware will run a pared-down version of visionOS 28 on a custom watch-derived chip and rely heavily on Siri AI and developer app integrations rather than opening separate phone apps.
Involved competitors include Apple, Meta (Ray-Ban smart glasses), and Google.
This matters because Apple plans to leverage its App Store ecosystem and advanced Visual Intelligence features to differentiate its wearable device from existing market rivals.
sentences: Apple wants to enter the smart glasses market.
The company is said to be working on its own pair of smart glasses for a while now as it plans to take on the Meta Ray-Bans.
As Apple gets closer to bringing its smart glasses to stores, it seems to be giving more focus to one feature – Siri AI.
As per a report from Bloomberg, Apple is planning to use Siri AI as a way for users to interact with its smart glasses.

The smart glasses, internally code-named N50, are expected to be similar to other smart glasses, comprising cameras, mics, and speakers. advertisement ❮ ❯ Using Siri AI for smart glasses The company is reportedly counting on its developer ecosystem to distinguish the glasses from rivals.
Apple wants developers to make specific functions within their existing iPhone apps accessible to Siri, allowing users to complete tasks without opening the apps or reaching for their phones.
The report said that Apple began laying the groundwork with the first beta version of iOS 27.3, adding a Siri function first promised in 2024.
The feature, rebuilt using new AI models, allows Siri to control apps and individual functions through voice commands and its chatbot interface.
Precise controls for Apple's apps are planned for the iOS 27.3 release in December, while wider third-party support is expected next year.

If accurate, it could allow for multiple use cases, such as asking Siri to reserve a table at a restaurant or book a cab.
The report says that the glasses will come with Wi-Fi support, allowing you to access some third-party app features even when your paired iPhone is not nearby.
It is believed that Android phones will not be supported.
Apple believes its App Store could give it an advantage over Meta's Muse agent and Google's Android ecosystem.
However, Meta and OpenAI are developing AI agents and third-party service integrations, while G oogle is using Gemini and Android XR to enable interactions with applications through smart glasses.

“AirPods for your face”
While Apple is rumoured to be working on more than one pair of smart glasses, the first model is not expected to include an augmented reality display.

The report says that this has led to employees describing it as “AirPods for your face.”
Internal prototypes run a pared-down version of visionOS 28 from the Vision Pro and use a custom processor derived from older Apple Watch chips.
They are slightly thinner than Meta's second-generation Ray-Ban glasses and feature flush, oval camera openings and a front indicator light.
You can also expect multiple colour options for the glasses.

Apple's glasses will use Visual Intelligence – from the cameras – to identify buildings, suggest meals based on ingredients visible in a refrigerator, translate conversations and signs, and answer questions about nearby objects.
They will also support navigation, calls, messages, notifications, calendars, reminders, music and smart-home controls.
Apple is also testing privacy safeguards, including on-device processing, limits on recording and facial recognition, and camera configurations intended only for sensing.
Privacy has become a major concern when it comes to smart glasses.
The Meta Ray-Bans have infamously gained the nickname “perv-glasses” as they let some users record others in public.
Though Mark Zuckerberg recently launched a version of the smart glasses without cameras.
The N50 hardware is largely finalised, but software development remains behind schedule and delays are possible, the report says.
It is expected that Apple will first showcase the smart glasses during WWDC 2027 in June next year.
